question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,v.$ Find $(u-2w)\cdot (w-4v).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot v=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u-2w)\cdot (w-4v) & =u\cdot w-2(w\cdot w)-4(u\cdot v)+8(w\cdot v) \\  & =u\cdot w-2(w\cdot w)+0+8(w\cdot v) \\  & =(1\cdot 3+4\cdot (-2)+(-2)\cdot 1+3\cdot 2) \\  & -2(3\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 1+2\cdot 2) \\  & +8(3\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 2+2\cdot 2) \\  & =(3-8-2+6)-2(9+4+1+4)+8(6+2+2+4) \\  & =-1-36+112 \\  & =75.\end{aligned}
$$
